newsitem.title: USA: Conrail group seeks all-cash payment.
newsitem.headline: Conrail group seeks all-cash payment.

text.p: A group of Conrail shareholders seeking to block the railroad's proposed merger with CSX Corp. asked a federal court to declare that CSX must pay $110 per share cash on demand for all Conrail shares.

The group said the combined stake of Conrail shares held by CSX and board members of Conrail exceeded the 20 percent threshold which, under a Pennsylvania law, triggers an obligation by an acquiring firm to pay "fair value" for all remaining shares of the firm.

The group also asked the U.S. District Court for Eastern Pennsylvania to prevent the Philadelphia-based railroad from postponing a Dec. 23 meeting at which shareholders will be asked to waive the law and allow the proposed merger -- a 40 percent cash, 60 percent stock deal -- to proceed.
The group is seeking to force Conrail to consider Norfolk, Va.-based Norfolk Southern Corp.'s all-cash $110-a-share offer for Conrail.
A Conrail spokeswoman said the filing, an amendment to an earlier lawsuit seeking to block the merger, was "frivolous and without merit."
Conrail has said it could postpone the meeting if it had not secured the votes to approve the waiver.

The shareholders group said in its court filing that the law should be triggered because Richmond, Va.-based CSX, which acquired 19.9 percent of Conrail shares in a $110 per share cash offer, should be considered as acting in concert with Conrail's board members, who approved the merger deal.
When the holdings are added together, the stake exceeds the 20 percent threshold level that triggers the law, the group said.
